# Plan: Add Concept of Scripts or Actions ## Overview Add the ability to define project-scoped scripts in `.mad/scripts.json` that can be triggered from the WebUI or TUI. Scripts are executed by an AI agent (not raw shell), which can work through issues autonomously. Output is streamed in real-time and captured to log files. --- ## 1. Script Configuration — `.mad/scripts.json` Create a new file `.mad/scripts.json` with this schema: ```json [ { "id": "deploy", "label": "Deploy to Production", "description": "Build and deploy the application to production", "command": "cd /home/paule/MAD && ./deploy.sh", "confirm": true, "model": null, "agent": null } ] ``` **Field definitions:** - `id` (string, required): Unique identifier, used in API calls and filenames. Must be alphanumeric + hyphens. - `label` (string, required): Human-readable name shown in UI. - `description` (string, optional): Explanation of what the script does. - `command` (string, required): The shell command or instructions for the agent to execute. - `confirm` (bool, optional, default: `true`): Whether to show a confirmation dialog before running. Defaults to true for safety — every script requires confirmation unless explicitly opted out. - `model` (string, optional): Override the agent model. If set, appended as `--model ` flag to the agent command. If null, uses the agent's default model. - `agent` (string, optional): Which configured agent to use (e.g., "claude", "opencode"). If null, uses `default_agent` from config. ### 1.1 Loading and Validation — `pipeline/scripts.py` (new file) ```python @dataclass class ScriptConfig: id: str label: str command: str description: str = "" confirm: bool = True model: Optional[str] = None agent: Optional[str] = None def load_scripts(mad_dir: Path) -> list[ScriptConfig]: scripts_path = mad_dir / "scripts.json" if not scripts_path.exists(): return [] data = json.loads(scripts_path.read_text()) scripts = [] seen_ids = set() for entry in data: # Validate required fields if not entry.get("id"): log.warning("Script entry missing 'id', skipping") continue if not entry.get("label"): log.warning(f"Script '{entry['id']}' missing 'label', skipping") continue if not entry.get("command"): log.warning(f"Script '{entry['id']}' missing 'command', skipping") continue if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$', entry['id']): log.warning(f"Script id '{entry['id']}' contains invalid characters, skipping") continue if entry['id'] in seen_ids: log.warning(f"Duplicate script id '{entry['id']}', skipping") continue seen_ids.add(entry['id']) scripts.append(ScriptConfig( id=entry['id'], label=entry['label'], command=entry['command'], description=entry.get('description', ''), confirm=entry.get('confirm', True), model=entry.get('model'), agent=entry.get('agent'), )) return scripts ``` --- ## 2. Script Execution — `pipeline/scripts.py` Scripts are executed by an AI agent in headless mode, similar to how planning/implementing phases work in `runner.py`. ### 2.1 ScriptStatus dataclass ```python @dataclass class ScriptStatus: script_id: str running: bool = False pid: Optional[int] = None started_at: Optional[str] = None finished_at: Optional[str] = None lines: list = field(default_factory=list) exit_code: Optional[int] = None kill_requested: bool = False # See §2.3 for thread safety context: str = "" # User-provided context ``` ### 2.2 run_script() function ```python async def run_script(script: ScriptConfig, config: Config, status: ScriptStatus, context: str = "") -> int: """ Execute a script via AI agent in headless mode. Returns exit code (0 = success). """ # 1. Determine agent agent_name = script.agent or config.raw.get('default_agent', 'claude') agent_config = config.agents[agent_name] runner = AgentRunner(config, agent_name, config.code_path) # 2. Build prompt prompt = f"""# Script Execution: {script.label} ## Task Execute the following command/task and handle any issues that arise: ``` {script.command} ``` {f'## Description{chr(10)}{script.description}' if script.description else ''} {f'## Additional Context{chr(10)}{context}' if context else ''} ## Instructions - Execute the command above - If errors occur, attempt to diagnose and fix them - Report the outcome clearly """ # 3. Model override # If script.model is set, temporarily override the agent's model. # AgentRunner.headless() constructs the command using agent_config.model: # cmd = [agent_config.command, agent_config.headless_flag, ...] # if agent_config.model: cmd.extend([agent_config.model_flag, agent_config.model]) # So setting agent_config.model before calling headless() will cause # --model to be appended to the agent command. original_model = agent_config.model if script.model: agent_config.model = script.model # 4. Execute via runner.headless() # Use phase_key=f"script-{script.id}" for file naming # The runner writes to .tmp/script-{script.id}.instructions # and reads from .tmp/script-{script.id}.output.json try: status.running = True status.started_at = datetime.now().isoformat() status.pid = None status.lines = [] output = runner.headless( prompt=prompt, workdir=config.code_path, status=status, phase_key=f"script-{script.id}", output_schema={"summary": "string", "success": "bool"}, ) status.exit_code = 0 return 0 except Exception as e: status.exit_code = 1 status.lines.append(f"Error: {e}") return 1 finally: if script.model: agent_config.model = original_model status.running = False status.finished_at = datetime.now().isoformat() # Write log to .mad/logs/script-{script.id}-{timestamp}.log _save_script_log(config, script, status) def _save_script_log(config: Config, script: ScriptConfig, status: ScriptStatus): log_dir = config.code_path / '.mad' / 'logs' log_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True) timestamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S') log_path = log_dir / f"script-{script.id}-{timestamp}.log" log_path.write_text('\n'.join(status.lines)) ``` ### 2.3 Thread Safety for kill_requested The `kill_requested` flag on `ScriptStatus` is accessed from two threads: - **Main TUI thread**: sets `kill_requested = True` when user cancels - **Worker thread** (via `@work(thread=True)`): reads `kill_requested` in the runner's polling loop This is safe because: 1. `kill_requested` is a simple boolean — Python's GIL guarantees atomic reads/writes of simple attributes. 2. This is the exact same pattern already used by `runner.py` (line ~395) where `status.kill_requested` is checked in the subprocess polling loop. The existing `_run_plan_async` and `_run_implement_async` workers in `tui.py` already set `kill_requested` from the main thread. 3. Textual's `@work(thread=True)` runs in a standard Python thread, so GIL protections apply. No additional synchronization (locks, events) is needed. This matches the established codebase pattern. --- ## 3. Server-Side Changes — `server/api.go` and `server/hub.go` ### 3.1 New HTTP Endpoint — `api.go` Add a new endpoint following the exact pattern of `serveStartAgent()` (api.go:643): ```go // POST /api/clients/{id}/run-script func (s *Server) serveRunScript(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { if r.Method != http.MethodPost { http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", 405) return } if !s.checkAuth(r, w) { return } clientID := r.PathValue("id") // Parse request body var req struct { ScriptID string `json:"script_id"` Context string `json:"context"` } if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil { http.Error(w, "Bad request", 400) return } if req.ScriptID == "" { http.Error(w, "script_id required", 400) return } // Send run_script message to pipeline client via WebSocket msg := map[string]interface{}{ "type": "run_script", "script_id": req.ScriptID, "context": req.Context, } msgBytes, _ := json.Marshal(msg) s.hub.SendToClient(clientID, msgBytes) w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{"status": "sent"}) } ``` **Register the route** (in the same place as other routes, around api.go:200): ```go mux.HandleFunc("/api/clients/{id}/run-script", s.serveRunScript) ``` **Message flow (addressing the forwarding concern):** ``` WebUI (browser) → POST /api/clients/{id}/run-script → serveRunScript() validates auth and body → hub.SendToClient(clientID, msgBytes) → Client.send channel → writePump() → WebSocket → Python ServerClient._handle_incoming() receives "run_script" message → dispatches to on_run_script callback → TUI executes script ``` This does NOT go through hub.handleMessage() at all. The HTTP endpoint sends directly to the client's WebSocket via SendToClient(), which is a direct channel write — same pattern as serveStartAgent(), serveAnswerQuestions(), and all other existing server→client commands. ### 3.2 No hub.go Message Routing Changes Needed The `run_script` message does NOT flow through hub.handleMessage()'s switch statement (lines 305-307). It is sent via the HTTP endpoint → SendToClient() path, which bypasses message routing entirely. This is identical to how `start_agent`, `answer_questions`, `move_feature`, etc. all work. ### 3.3 State Struct Extensions — `hub.go` Extend `ClientState` to include script information passed through from push_state(): ```go type ScriptInfo struct { ID string `json:"id"` Label string `json:"label"` Description string `json:"description"` Confirm bool `json:"confirm"` } type ScriptState struct { ScriptID string `json:"script_id"` Running bool `json:"running"` Lines []string `json:"lines"` StartedAt string `json:"started_at,omitempty"` FinishedAt string `json:"finished_at,omitempty"` ExitCode *int `json:"exit_code,omitempty"` } ``` Add to `ClientState`: ```go Scripts []ScriptInfo `json:"scripts,omitempty"` ScriptStatus *ScriptState `json:"script_status,omitempty"` ``` These fields are populated by the pipeline client's `push_state()` call — the server just stores and forwards them, no server-side logic needed. --- ## 4. Pipeline Client Changes — `pipeline/server_client.py` ### 4.1 New Callback Add `on_run_script` callback to `ServerClient.__init__()`: ```python def __init__(self, ..., on_run_script=None): self.on_run_script = on_run_script ``` ### 4.2 Message Handling In `_handle_incoming()`, add a new case in the message type dispatch: ```python elif msg_type == "run_script": script_id = data.get("script_id", "") context = data.get("context", "") if self.on_run_script: await self.on_run_script(script_id, context) ``` ### 4.3 State Pushing In `push_state()`, add script data to the state payload: ```python def push_state(self, features, plan_status, impl_status, auto_plan_enabled, auto_impl_enabled, scripts=None, script_status=None): # New params # ... existing code ... state["scripts"] = [ {"id": s.id, "label": s.label, "description": s.description, "confirm": s.confirm} for s in (scripts or []) ] if script_status and script_status.running: state["script_status"] = { "script_id": script_status.script_id, "running": script_status.running, "lines": script_status.lines[-50:], # Last 50 lines for WebUI "started_at": script_status.started_at, "finished_at": script_status.finished_at, "exit_code": script_status.exit_code, } ``` --- ## 5. TUI Changes — `pipeline/tui.py` ### 5.1 Script State in PipelineApp Add to `PipelineApp.__init__()` or class body: ```python self._scripts: list[ScriptConfig] = load_scripts(self.mad_dir) self._script_status: Optional[ScriptStatus] = None ``` ### 5.2 Script List UI Add a "Scripts" section to the sidebar or as a new keybinding (e.g., `S` for Scripts). Show available scripts with their labels. ### 5.3 Run Script Modal — `RunScriptModal` New modal extending `ModalScreen`: ```python class RunScriptModal(ModalScreen[Optional[tuple[str, str]]]): """Modal to select and run a script.""" BINDINGS = [("escape", "cancel", "Cancel")] def __init__(self, scripts: list[ScriptConfig]): super().__init__() self.scripts = scripts def compose(self): with Vertical(id="modal-dialog"): yield Static("Run Script", classes="modal-title") yield Select( [(s.label, s.id) for s in self.scripts], prompt="Select script", id="script-select", ) yield TextArea(id="script-context", placeholder="Additional context for the agent (optional)") yield Horizontal( Button("Run", variant="primary", id="run-btn"), Button("Cancel", variant="default", id="cancel-btn"), ) def on_button_pressed(self, event): if event.button.id == "run-btn": script_id = self.query_one("#script-select").value context = self.query_one("#script-context").text if script_id: selected = next(s for s in self.scripts if s.id == script_id) if selected.confirm: # Show confirmation self.app.push_screen( ConfirmModal(f"Run '{selected.label}'?"), callback=lambda ok: self.dismiss((script_id, context)) if ok else None ) else: self.dismiss((script_id, context)) elif event.button.id == "cancel-btn": self.dismiss(None) ``` ### 5.4 Script Execution Worker ```python @work(thread=True, exclusive=True, group="script") async def _run_script_async(self, script_id: str, context: str = ""): script = next((s for s in self._scripts if s.id == script_id), None) if not script: self.notify(f"Script '{script_id}' not found", severity="error") return self._script_status = ScriptStatus(script_id=script_id, context=context) try: exit_code = await run_script(script, self.config, self._script_status, context) self.app.call_from_thread( self.notify, f"Script '{script.label}' finished (exit code: {exit_code})", severity="information" if exit_code == 0 else "error", ) except Exception as e: self.app.call_from_thread( self.notify, f"Script error: {e}", severity="error" ) finally: self._script_status = None ``` ### 5.5 Server Callback Wiring In `_connect_server()`, add the callback: ```python self.server_client = ServerClient( ..., on_run_script=self._handle_run_script, ) async def _handle_run_script(self, script_id: str, context: str): """Called when WebUI requests script execution.""" script = next((s for s in self._scripts if s.id == script_id), None) if not script: return # Scripts triggered from WebUI skip TUI confirmation since WebUI has its own self._run_script_async(script_id, context) ``` ### 5.6 Push Script State to Server In `_push_to_server()`, pass script data: ```python self.server_client.push_state( ..., scripts=self._scripts, script_status=self._script_status, ) ``` ### 5.7 Kill Running Script Add keybinding (e.g., `K` when script is running): ```python def action_kill_script(self): if self._script_status and self._script_status.running: self._script_status.kill_requested = True self.notify("Kill requested for running script") ``` --- ## 6. WebUI Changes — `server/templates/client.html` The active template is `client.html` (loaded in api.go:204 via `template.Must(template.New("").Funcs(funcMap).ParseFS(templateFS, "templates/index.html", "templates/client.html"))`). ### 6.1 Scripts Panel Add a "Scripts" section to the client detail page, after the features section: ```html

Scripts

Script Output


        

    



```

### 6.2 JavaScript for Script Management

```javascript
function renderScripts(clientId, scripts, scriptStatus) {
    const section = document.getElementById('scripts-section');
    const list = document.getElementById('scripts-list');
    if (!scripts || scripts.length === 0) {
        section.style.display = 'none';
        return;
    }
    section.style.display = 'block';
    list.innerHTML = scripts.map(s => `
        

            ${escapeHtml(s.label)}
            ${s.description ? `
${escapeHtml(s.description)}
` : ''}
            
        

    `).join('');

    // Show live output if script is running
    if (scriptStatus?.running) {
        showScriptOutput(scriptStatus);
    }
}

function runScript(clientId, scriptId, requireConfirm) {
    let context = '';
    // Always prompt for optional context
    context = prompt('Additional context for the agent (optional):') ?? '';
    
    if (requireConfirm) {
        if (!confirm(`Run script '${scriptId}'?`)) return;
    }

    fetch(`/api/clients/${encodeURIComponent(clientId)}/run-script?key=${encodeURIComponent(dashboardKey)}`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
        body: JSON.stringify({
            script_id: scriptId,
            context: context,
        }),
    });
}

function showScriptOutput(status) {
    const modal = document.getElementById('script-output-modal');
    const log = document.getElementById('script-output-log');
    const indicator = document.getElementById('script-status-indicator');
    modal.style.display = 'block';
    log.textContent = status.lines.join('\n');
    log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight;  // Auto-scroll
    indicator.textContent = status.running ? 'Running...' : 
        (status.exit_code === 0 ? 'Completed' : 'Failed');
}
```

### 6.3 Integration with Existing State Updates

The WebUI already receives state updates via WebSocket polling. The `scripts` and `script_status` fields added to `ClientState` will automatically flow through. In the existing `updateClientDetail()` function (or equivalent), add:

```javascript
renderScripts(clientId, state.scripts, state.script_status);
```

Streaming output works because `push_state()` runs every 10 seconds (configurable via `push_interval_seconds`). For near-real-time streaming, the output updates every push interval. The last 50 lines are sent each push to keep payload size manageable.

---

## 7. Implementation Order

1. **`pipeline/scripts.py`** — ScriptConfig, ScriptStatus, load_scripts(), run_script(), _save_script_log()
2. **`pipeline/server_client.py`** — Add on_run_script callback, handle run_script message, extend push_state()
3. **`server/api.go`** — Add /api/clients/{id}/run-script endpoint
4. **`server/hub.go`** — Add ScriptInfo, ScriptState structs to ClientState
5. **`pipeline/tui.py`** — Load scripts, add RunScriptModal, add _run_script_async worker, wire callbacks, add keybindings
6. **`server/templates/client.html`** — Add scripts section, script output modal, JavaScript
7. **`.mad/scripts.json`** — Create example configuration
8. **Testing** — Manual test: add a test script, trigger from TUI and WebUI, verify streaming output

## 8. Files Modified

- `pipeline/scripts.py` (NEW)
- `pipeline/server_client.py` (MODIFIED)
- `pipeline/tui.py` (MODIFIED)
- `pipeline/runner.py` (no changes needed — reuse existing AgentRunner)
- `server/api.go` (MODIFIED)
- `server/hub.go` (MODIFIED)
- `server/templates/client.html` (MODIFIED)
- `.mad/scripts.json` (NEW)

## 9. Out of Scope

- Auto-triggering scripts on stage transitions (future)
- Editing scripts from WebUI (scripts.json is file-only)
- Script scheduling / cron
- Per-board script scoping (all scripts are project-scoped)
- Script dependencies / chaining

# Test Spec: Add Concept of Scripts or Actions

## 1. Behaviors That MUST Be Verified

### 1.1 Script Configuration Loading (`pipeline/scripts.py` — `load_scripts()`)

**Behavior:** Loading a valid `scripts.json` returns a list of ScriptConfig objects with correct field values.
- Given a `.mad/scripts.json` with one entry containing all fields (id, label, command, description, confirm, model, agent), `load_scripts()` returns a list with one ScriptConfig whose attributes match the JSON values exactly.

**Behavior:** Missing `scripts.json` returns an empty list.
- Given no `.mad/scripts.json` file exists, `load_scripts()` returns `[]` without error.

**Behavior:** Required field validation skips invalid entries.
- An entry missing `id` is skipped (warning logged).
- An entry missing `label` is skipped (warning logged).
- An entry missing `command` is skipped (warning logged).
- Valid entries in the same file are still loaded.

**Behavior:** ID format validation rejects invalid characters.
- An entry with id `"my script!"` (contains space and exclamation) is skipped.
- An entry with id `"my_script"` (contains underscore) is skipped.
- An entry with id `"my-script"` (alphanumeric + hyphens) is accepted.
- An entry with id `"MyScript123"` (mixed case alphanumeric) is accepted.

**Behavior:** Duplicate IDs are rejected.
- Given two entries with the same `id`, only the first is loaded; the second is skipped with a warning.

**Behavior:** Optional fields have correct defaults.
- An entry with only id, label, command results in: `description=""`, `confirm=True`, `model=None`, `agent=None`.

**Behavior:** `confirm` defaults to True.
- An entry without a `confirm` field has `confirm=True`.
- An entry with `"confirm": false` has `confirm=False`.

### 1.2 Script Execution (`pipeline/scripts.py` — `run_script()`)

**Behavior:** Successful script execution returns exit code 0.
- Given a valid ScriptConfig and a mock runner whose `headless()` returns successfully, `run_script()` returns 0 and `status.exit_code` is 0.

**Behavior:** Failed script execution returns exit code 1.
- Given a ScriptConfig where `runner.headless()` raises an exception, `run_script()` returns 1, `status.exit_code` is 1, and the error message is appended to `status.lines`.

**Behavior:** Status lifecycle is correct.
- Before execution: `status.running` is False.
- During execution: `status.running` is True, `status.started_at` is set to an ISO timestamp.
- After execution (success or failure): `status.running` is False, `status.finished_at` is set.

**Behavior:** Model override is applied and restored.
- Given `script.model = "claude-sonnet"` and `agent_config.model = "claude-opus"`, during execution the agent_config.model is `"claude-sonnet"`. After execution (success or failure), `agent_config.model` is restored to `"claude-opus"`.

**Behavior:** Model override restoration on exception.
- If `runner.headless()` raises, `agent_config.model` is still restored to its original value.

**Behavior:** Agent selection uses script.agent or config default.
- If `script.agent` is set to `"opencode"`, the runner uses agent `"opencode"`.
- If `script.agent` is None, the runner uses `config.raw['default_agent']` (or `'claude'` if not set).

**Behavior:** Prompt includes script details.
- The prompt passed to `runner.headless()` contains the script's label, command, description (if present), and context (if provided).
- If description is empty, the description section is omitted from the prompt.
- If context is empty, the context section is omitted from the prompt.

**Behavior:** Log file is saved after execution.
- After `run_script()` completes, a log file exists at `.mad/logs/script-{id}-{YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS}.log` containing the output lines joined by newlines.

**Behavior:** Kill propagation works.
- Setting `status.kill_requested = True` propagates to the inner `_agent_status.kill_requested`, allowing the subprocess to be terminated.

### 1.3 Server Client (`pipeline/server_client.py`)

**Behavior:** `run_script` message dispatches to callback.
- When a WebSocket message `{"type": "run_script", "script_id": "deploy", "context": "hotfix"}` is received, `on_run_script` is called with `("deploy", "hotfix")`.

**Behavior:** Missing callback is handled gracefully.
- If `on_run_script` is None and a `run_script` message arrives, no error is raised.

**Behavior:** `push_state()` includes scripts array.
- When `scripts` parameter is provided, the state message contains a `scripts` key with an array of `{id, label, description, confirm}` objects.

**Behavior:** `push_state()` includes script_status when running.
- When `script_status` is provided and running, the state message contains `script_status` with `script_id`, `running`, `lines` (last 50), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `exit_code`.

**Behavior:** Lines are truncated to last 50 in push_state.
- If `script_status.lines` has 100 entries, only the last 50 are included in the state message.

**Behavior:** No scripts or script_status when not provided.
- When `scripts=None` and `script_status=None`, the state message does not contain these keys (or contains empty/null values).

### 1.4 Go Server — API Endpoint (`server/api.go`)

**Behavior:** POST `/api/clients/{id}/run-script` sends message to client.
- Given a connected client, POST with `{"script_id": "deploy", "context": "hotfix"}` results in a `{"type": "run_script", "script_id": "deploy", "context": "hotfix"}` message being sent to the client's WebSocket.
- Response is 200 with `{"status": "ok"}`.

**Behavior:** Missing script_id returns 400.
- POST with `{"script_id": ""}` or `{}` returns 400 with error message.

**Behavior:** Non-POST method returns 405.
- GET `/api/clients/{id}/run-script` returns 405.

**Behavior:** Unauthenticated request is rejected.
- POST without valid auth key returns 401/403.

**Behavior:** Invalid JSON body returns 400.
- POST with malformed body returns 400.

### 1.5 Go Server — State Structs (`server/hub.go`)

**Behavior:** ScriptInfo and ScriptState fields are parsed from state_update.
- When a pipeline client sends a `state_update` message with `scripts` and `script_status` fields, these are correctly parsed into `ClientState.Scripts` and `ClientState.ScriptStatus`.

**Behavior:** ScriptStatus with exit_code null is handled.
- When `script_status.exit_code` is null in JSON, `ScriptState.ExitCode` is nil (pointer type).

**Behavior:** Missing scripts field results in empty/nil.
- A `state_update` without `scripts` or `script_status` fields leaves those ClientState fields as their zero values.

### 1.6 TUI Integration (`pipeline/tui.py`)

**Behavior:** Scripts are loaded at startup.
- `PipelineApp._scripts` is populated from `.mad/scripts.json` during initialization.

**Behavior:** "S" keybinding opens RunScriptModal.
- Pressing S (or configured key) when scripts are configured opens the modal with script options.

**Behavior:** No-scripts notification.
- If no scripts are configured, pressing S shows a notification "No scripts configured".

**Behavior:** Already-running guard.
- If a script is already running, pressing S shows "A script is already running" instead of opening the modal.

**Behavior:** RunScriptModal shows all scripts.
- The modal's Select dropdown contains all loaded scripts with their labels.

**Behavior:** Confirmation dialog shown when confirm=true.
- Selecting a script with `confirm=true` and clicking Run shows a confirmation dialog before execution.

**Behavior:** No confirmation when confirm=false.
- Selecting a script with `confirm=false` and clicking Run starts execution immediately.

**Behavior:** Cancel dismisses modal.
- Clicking Cancel or pressing Escape dismisses the modal without running anything.

**Behavior:** Script status is pushed to server.
- While a script is running, `_push_to_server()` includes `scripts` and `script_status` in the state pushed to the server.

**Behavior:** WebUI-triggered scripts skip TUI confirmation.
- When `_handle_run_script` is called from server callback, the script runs directly without TUI confirmation (WebUI has its own confirmation).

**Behavior:** Kill action terminates running script.
- When a script is running, the kill action sets `kill_requested=True` on the script status, which propagates to the agent subprocess.

### 1.7 WebUI (`server/templates/client.html`)

**Behavior:** Scripts section is visible when scripts exist.
- When state includes non-empty `scripts` array, the scripts section is displayed.

**Behavior:** Scripts section is hidden when no scripts.
- When state has no `scripts` or empty array, the scripts section is hidden.

**Behavior:** Run button triggers API call.
- Clicking Run on a script card sends POST to `/api/clients/{id}/run-script` with the script_id and optional context.

**Behavior:** Confirmation prompt shown for confirm=true scripts.
- When a script has `confirm=true`, a browser confirm dialog appears before the API call.

**Behavior:** Context prompt is shown.
- Before running, a prompt dialog asks for optional additional context.

**Behavior:** Running script disables buttons.
- While `script_status.running` is true, all Run buttons are disabled.

**Behavior:** Live output displayed during execution.
- When `script_status` is present and running, the output modal shows the last lines with auto-scroll.

**Behavior:** Status indicator shows correct state.
- Running: shows "Running..."
- Completed (exit_code 0): shows "Completed"
- Failed (exit_code != 0): shows "Failed"

---

## 2. Edge Cases

### 2.1 Empty/Null Inputs
- `scripts.json` is an empty array `[]` — returns empty list, no errors.
- `scripts.json` contains `null` — handles gracefully (returns empty list or logs warning).
- `scripts.json` is not valid JSON — logs error, returns empty list.
- Script entry has `"description": null` — treated as empty string.
- Script entry has `"model": ""` — treated as no model override (empty string = no override).
- Context passed to `run_script()` is empty string — no context section in prompt.
- Context passed to `run_script()` is None — no context section in prompt.

### 2.2 Boundary Conditions
- Script with very long command string (10K+ chars) — should work, passed through to agent.
- Script ID at edge of valid pattern: single char `"a"`, very long `"a-b-c-d-e-f-g-h-i-j"` — both accepted.
- 50+ scripts in `scripts.json` — all loaded, all shown in modal/WebUI.
- `status.lines` with exactly 50 entries — all 50 sent in push_state.
- `status.lines` with 51 entries — only last 50 sent.
- `status.lines` empty — empty array sent.

### 2.3 Invalid States
- `scripts.json` exists but is not an array (e.g., object `{}`) — handles gracefully.
- Agent name in script.agent doesn't exist in config.agents — appropriate error raised/handled.
- Client ID in run-script API doesn't exist — message send fails gracefully (no crash).
- Client disconnects while script is running — script continues to completion, status is preserved.

### 2.4 Concurrent Operations
- Running a script while a plan/implement agent is also running — both should coexist.
- Two rapid run-script API calls — second should be rejected (already running guard).
- Push state while script is running and lines are being appended — thread-safe read of lines list.
- Kill requested while script output is being streamed — kill propagates, script terminates.

### 2.5 Error Conditions
- `runner.headless()` throws exception — caught, exit_code=1, error in lines, model restored.
- `.mad/logs/` directory doesn't exist — created by `_save_script_log()` (mkdir exist_ok).
- Log file write fails (permissions) — should not crash the application.
- WebSocket disconnected when run_script message arrives — handled gracefully.
- `scripts.json` has BOM or unusual encoding — handled or fails gracefully.

---

## 3. What Constitutes Failure

### 3.1 Script Loading Failures
- FAIL: `load_scripts()` raises an unhandled exception for any malformed input.
- FAIL: Valid entries are not loaded because an invalid entry earlier in the list caused a crash.
- FAIL: Duplicate ID entries are both loaded instead of the second being skipped.
- FAIL: An entry with invalid ID format (e.g., containing underscores or spaces) is accepted.

### 3.2 Script Execution Failures
- FAIL: `status.running` remains True after `run_script()` returns.
- FAIL: `agent_config.model` is not restored after an exception during execution.
- FAIL: `status.started_at` or `status.finished_at` is not set after execution.
- FAIL: Log file is not written after execution.
- FAIL: `run_script()` raises an unhandled exception to the caller (should always return 0 or 1).

### 3.3 Server Failures
- FAIL: POST to `/api/clients/{id}/run-script` returns 500 for valid input.
- FAIL: State update with `scripts`/`script_status` causes server crash or JSON parse error.
- FAIL: `ScriptState.ExitCode` cannot represent null (must be pointer type).

### 3.4 TUI Failures
- FAIL: Pressing S when no scripts configured causes crash instead of showing notification.
- FAIL: RunScriptModal doesn't dismiss on Cancel or Escape.
- FAIL: Two scripts can run simultaneously (missing already-running guard).
- FAIL: Script status is not included in push_state during execution.

### 3.5 WebUI Failures
- FAIL: Scripts section appears when there are no scripts.
- FAIL: Run button still active while a script is running.
- FAIL: XSS vulnerability via script label or description (must be escaped in HTML rendering).
- FAIL: API call missing auth key.

### 3.6 Integration Failures
- FAIL: Full flow (WebUI click → API → WebSocket → Python callback → execution → status push → WebUI display) doesn't complete end-to-end.
- FAIL: Script output lines are never visible in WebUI during execution.
- FAIL: Kill from TUI doesn't terminate the running script agent.

---

## 4. Out of Scope

- **Visual/UI assertions:** Exact styling, colors, layout positioning, CSS classes of script cards or modals.
- **Performance benchmarks:** How fast scripts load, execute, or how quickly output streams.
- **UI timing:** Exact timing of HTMX/WebSocket polling intervals, animation durations.
- **Agent behavior:** Whether the AI agent actually executes the command correctly — only that the agent is invoked with the right prompt.
- **Script content:** Testing specific shell commands or their outcomes — only that the execution framework works.
- **Auto-triggering:** Scripts triggered by stage transitions (explicitly out of scope per plan).
- **WebUI script editing:** Editing scripts.json from the browser (out of scope per plan).
- **Script scheduling/cron:** Timed or periodic script execution.
- **Per-board scoping:** Scripts scoped to specific boards.
- **Script dependencies/chaining:** Running scripts in sequence or with dependencies.
- **Browser compatibility:** Testing across different browsers or browser versions.
- **Load testing:** Multiple simultaneous WebUI users triggering scripts.
- **File system permissions:** Testing with read-only `.mad/` directories (beyond basic error handling).
- **Agent model availability:** Whether the specified model actually exists or is accessible.

questions.question: Where should scripts be defined? Options: (a) in .mad/config.json under a new 'scripts' key, (b) in a separate .mad/scripts.json file, or (c) as actual shell script files in a .mad/scripts/ directory with metadata.
Should scripts be scoped globally (available to all boards) or per-board? For example, a 'deploy' script might only apply to the 'mad' board.
questions.answer: I think they are project-scoped, so they can be available in all boards, I think.  Boards are just ways to organize ideas for a project.

questions.question: Should scripts receive feature context when triggered? E.g., if you click 'deploy' on a specific feature, should the script receive the feature's title, slug, plan, etc. as environment variables or arguments?
questions.answer: I don't think we will be deploying a specific feature.  I think that we should be allowed to provide context though, optionally, and I would like it to be an agent that actually runs the script so that it can work through issues that arise as well.  If the agent needs more context, it can read it in as needed.

questions.question: Should scripts only be triggerable manually from the WebUI, or should there also be an option to auto-trigger scripts on stage transitions (e.g., automatically deploy when a feature reaches 'done')?
questions.answer: For now, let's only do it manually from the python TUI or from the webui.  We may want to do things automatically, eventually, but not yet.

questions.question: What level of output feedback do you want in the WebUI? Options: (a) just success/failure status, (b) full streaming output visible in real-time, or (c) output captured and viewable after completion (like the existing log ring buffer).
questions.answer: Streaming output in real time would be great!  But we should capture the output in a log file as well.

questions.question: Should there be any safety controls? E.g., a confirmation dialog in the WebUI before running a script, or a whitelist of allowed scripts that can't be modified from the WebUI (only from config files on the local machine).
questions.answer: Confirmation in the webui is good.  No scripts should be modifiable via the webui, just executable.  Probably prompt for additional context to provide to the AI agent as well.
